# Motion Canvas API catalog (v3, verified against docs + template)

Pinned: `@motion-canvas/*` v3.17.2, scaffold `npm init @motion-canvas@latest`, template `template-2d-ts`.

## Project shape (generated by scaffolder)

```
<slug>/
  package.json          # scripts: start|serve (vite editor), build (tsc && vite build)
  vite.config.ts        # generated: motionCanvas() + ffmpeg() plugins
  tsconfig.json
  src/
    project.ts          # makeProject({scenes: [...]}) — scenes imported with ?scene
    scenes/*.tsx        # one makeScene2D per file
  output/               # RENDER frames land here (gitignore this)
```

`src/project.ts`:
```ts
import {makeProject} from '@motion-canvas/core';
import example from './scenes/example?scene';   // ?scene suffix is mandatory

export default makeProject({scenes: [example]});
```

## Scene skeleton (v3 barrel imports — NOT deep lib paths)

```tsx
import {Circle, makeScene2D} from '@motion-canvas/2d';
import {createRef} from '@motion-canvas/core';

export default makeScene2D(function* (view) {
  const circle = createRef<Circle>();
  view.add(<Circle ref={circle} size={320} fill={'lightseagreen'} />);
  yield* circle().scale(2, 2).to(1, 2);   // tween to 2 over 2s, back to 1 over 2s
});
```

## Core mechanics (quickstart-verified)

- **Generator flow**: the scene function is a generator; `yield*` plays an instruction to completion before continuing. No `yield*` = instant set, no animation.
- **Refs**: `createRef<T>()` + `ref={...}` attribute, dereference with `myRef()` to read/tween.
- **Tweens**: `node().prop(value, seconds)` transitions over time; `.to(value, seconds)` chains a follow-up on the same tween. Omitting seconds sets instantly.
- **Parallel**: `yield* all(a(...), b(...))` from `@motion-canvas/core` merges animations to run together.
- **Waiting**: `yield* waitFor(seconds)` from `@motion-canvas/core` holds the playhead (verified by compile, not quickstart page).
- **View**: `view.add(<Node/>)`; `view.fill(color)` sets scene background (the project background itself is NOT animatable).

## Flow helpers (`@motion-canvas/core`)

`all(...)` run together. `sequence(delay, ...anims)` staggers starts (verified by compile). `waitFor(s)` / `waitUntil(eventName)` pause. Prefer `sequence` over manual `all` + offsets for staggered charts.

## Easing

Pass as tween option, e.g. `rect().width(600, 1, easeOutCubic)` with `easeOutCubic` from `@motion-canvas/core`. Default easing is fine for drafts; set explicit easings for finals.

## Common 2D nodes (`@motion-canvas/2d`)

`Circle` (`size` shorthand for width+height), `Rect` (`width/height/radius/fill`), `Txt` (`text/fontSize/fontWeight/fill`), `Line` (`points`). Positioning: `x/y` absolute from center, or layout containers (`docs/layouts`). Text needs no LaTeX install — it renders with system/browser fonts; check glyph coverage for math symbols.

## Video Settings (render panel — editor, Video Settings tab)

`background` (base clear color; empty = transparent), `range` (frame span to render — use for drafts), `resolution` (px per frame; elements do NOT rescale — plan ahead), `scale` (rescales elements too — prefer over resolution for size changes), `frame rate` (24/30/60; animations are fps-resilient), `quality` (0-1, ignored for PNG), `file type` (PNG/JPEG/WebP; WebP broken on Safari/old browsers), `color space` (sRGB default). Preview and render have independent scale/fps — keep preview light, render heavy.

## Exporters

- **Image sequence** (always on): RENDER writes frames to `output/` in the project dir.
- **Video (FFmpeg)**: `npm install --save @motion-canvas/ffmpeg` + add `ffmpeg()` to `vite.config.ts` plugins. You do NOT install FFmpeg yourself — the exporter bundles its binary. Options: include audio (needs `docs/media` audio setup), fast start (web streaming optimization). Select it in the Video Settings tab.

## npm scripts (template)

`npm run serve` (alias `start`) = editor at http://localhost:9000. `npm run build` = `tsc && vite build` — the cheap gate: catches type errors before any render. There is NO template render script; rendering is driven per SKILL.md workflow.
